independentMethod: PCM decoded with wave; signed carrier-maxima log regression; explicit observation matrices and exact PCM rivals. No producer numerical module imported.
acceptedClaim: Given known stable reference, separated channels, physical-time premise and common scalar gain, slope difference identifies target amplitude decay in the finite synthetic model.
limitations: Reference stability and shared gain are premises, not identified from corrected residuals.
Differential gain or unstable reference restores a nontrivial kernel; exact same-PCM examples with alpha 4 and 5 per second were executed.
The two channels already separate the signals; a one-microphone decomposition is not demonstrated.
Generated stereo PCM and digital full scale are not measured pressure, physical damping or energy.
No noise coverage or empirical calibration threshold was established.

sourceChecks.read: autoGainControl capability and constrainable property entries
sourceChecks.supports: Controls/reporting exist; they do not establish calibrated acoustic response.
A concrete speech-processing architecture uses time-frequency operations. This does not establish that a given capture device obeys that architecture or a scalar gain law.

nextQuestion: How should a repeatable low-material pilot distinguish a practically usable slope difference from noisy or model-mismatched reference estimates, without treating uncertainty under the shared model as a bound on unmeasured differential gain?
